In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention of HIV transmission in the context of a large epidemic in Edinburgh and Scotland.
the provision of sterile injection equipment for the prevention of HIV infection among drug injectors.
the prevention of HIV and hepatitis B virus infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the United States has been slow to respond to the HIV epidemic among injection drugs users.
the provision of injection paraphernalia is a necessary part of a comprehensive harm-reduction program and that it has been shown to be safe and acceptable in many countries.
the provision of sterile equipment for injection drug users is a major public health measure to prevent the transmission of HIV and hepatitis C virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the United Kingdom has responded to the problem of HIV infection and the transmission of hepatitis C virus by providing sterile injection equipment to all those who need it, and the response has worked.
we are now at the stage of providing a comprehensive range of injection paraphernalia to injection drug users.
we are not yet at the stage of Burris and colleagues' program but are working to reach that goal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prescription of sterile equipment is only the beginning of the solution.
we need to be careful about what we prescribe, to whom we prescribe, how we prescribe, and how we monitor the effectiveness of the program.
we need to provide more injection equipment to injection drug users.
